title: Hybrid slab arena and adaptive checkpoint scheduler to reduce GPU workspace
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU workspace by ~28% and end-to-end GPU footprint by ~18% for typical chat workloads; no API changes. Rollout: gradual on Dedicated pools with new arena tunables defaulting to safe limits.
description: Summary: This PR introduces a hybrid slab-focused arena allocator plus an adaptive activation checkpoint scheduler that cooperates with per-kernel scratch throttling and KV-cache LRU hints to materially reduce peak workspace and overall device allocation for long-context chat workloads. Motivation: customers running 100k+ token sessions and multi-turn chat were hitting OOMs on medium GPUs due to worst-case scratch+arena peaks; previous approaches (pure checkpointing or global arena caps) either increased latency or underutilized GPU memory. The goal here is to reduce worst-case workspace while preserving p95/p99 latency and throughput. What changed: 1) Arena allocator: add slab reservation for transient kernel scratch (slab_reserve_ratio tunable) so short-lived scratch allocations get carved from a temporary slab instead of the global arena; introduce slab eviction heuristics to free slabs when sustained memory pressure detected. 2) Hybrid checkpoint scheduler: new scheduler defers some activation checkpoints from the hot microbatches to colder microbatches within the same request when safe, reducing simultaneous checkpoint buffers; it uses a cheap cost model keyed by sequence-length and layer-flops to decide which layers to checkpoint eagerly versus deferred. 3) Scratch pool throttling: per-kernel scratch quotas that bias kernel selection toward low-scratch variants under pressure; integrates with kernel selector to prefer fused-attention paths that use smaller temporary buffers when sequence-length distribution suggests benefit. 4) KV-cache coalescing: KV manager now coalesces identical prefix KV handles across concurrent requests from the same conversation id to avoid duplicate KV allocations; LRU hinting reduces retention of rarely-reused past-turn keys. 5) Runtime knobs and telemetry: new tunables (slab_reserve_ratio, checkpoint_deferral_threshold, scratch_quota_ms) and metrics (arena.slabs.active, checkpoint.deferrals, scratch.throttled_count) added to Console and traces. Benchmarks: Internal p50/p95/p99 latency changes on rw-llama-7b loadtest with batch=8 and 4 concurrent streams: peak device allocations down 28% (from 9.8GB to 7.0GB), average device footprint down 18%, p95 latency +2.3%, p99 latency +3.8% on worst-case mixed-length traces; throughput unchanged within noise. Safety/perf tradeoffs: some microbatched requests may force checkpoint deferral causing slightly higher recompute on tail cases; knobs default conservatively to minimize recompute for latency-sensitive tiers. Commits: "alloc: add slab reserve allocator and eviction policy"; "sched: hybrid checkpoint scheduler and cost model"; "kernel: scratch quota enforcement + selector hints"; "kv: coalesce conversation kv handles and LRU hints"; "telemetry: arena and scheduler metrics + console panels"; "tests: add unit/integration tests for slab/deferral behaviour". Files changed (high level): runtime/allocator/slab_arena.{h,cpp} - new slab reserve implementation; runtime/scheduler/checkpoint_scheduler.cpp - new scheduler and cost model; runtime/kernel/scratch_pool.cpp - quota enforcement and selector hooks; runtime/kv/kv_cache_manager.cpp - coalescing logic and LRU hint flow; runtime/selector/kernel_selector.cpp - prefer low-scratch kernel variants when quota triggered; console/metrics/arena_dashboards.yaml - new panels; tests/allocator/test_slab_eviction.cpp - unit tests; integration/bench/long_context_memory.yaml - benchmark harness. Small illustrative snippet (updated allocator heuristic): "if (current_pressure > slab_threshold) slab->evict_least_recently_used(); else reserve_from_slab(requested)". Review conversation: Jordan Kim (reviewer) requested clearer invariants around deferral: "How do we ensure correctness when deferring checkpoint writes across microbatches?"; Anika replied: "We only defer within the same parent request boundary and track dependency fences per-layer; added assertion coverage and integration tests to validate tensor liveness across deferral windows." Priya Desai asked for telemetry gating and signal names; Anika: "Added metrics and Console panels and documented tunables in runtime/README.md; default values set to conservative for hosted API." Liam O'Connor raised concern about KV coalescing for multi-tenant Dedicated pools: "Could coalescing leak state across tenants?"; response: "Coalescing keyed by conversation-id + tenant-id; no cross-tenant sharing. Added unit tests and an audit log entry when coalescing occurs." CI status: initial lint failure (allocator header include order), tests flaky on integration bench (timing sensitivity) causing a failed run; fixes applied and CI green on re-run. Rollout plan: feature gated under runtime.tunable.hybrid_checkpoint enabled=false by default for hosted main, enabled in internal perf clusters and Dedicated with opt-in; gradual rollout to all Dedicated pools after two-week soak. Related work: follows ENG-742 and builds on previous arena and checkpoint experiments (see PRs reducing arena/checkpoint footprint) but differs by combining slab-reservation with a cost-driven deferral scheduler and KV coalescing. Merge: squash and merged by Anika Rao; merge commit message: "hybrid slab arena + adaptive checkpoint scheduler - reduce workspace and scratch peaks". Notes for ops: if customers report increased recompute tail, recommend lowering checkpoint_deferral_threshold or disabling hybrid_checkpoint for that pool. Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] integration bench added, [x] telemetry panels, [x] docs updated, [x] feature gated for gradual rollout.
